source.title: Surface roughness prior for outdoor building materials at millimetre wave
source.model: coherent reflected power fraction = exp(-g^2), g = 4*pi*rms_height*cos(theta)/lambda
source.model_anchor: Recommendation ITU-R P.2146-0 equation 11 carries this factor as exp{-(2*k*s*cos(theta_i))^2}, which is identical, with s defined in its section 4.1 as the total RMS surface height. P.2146-0 is a sea-surface Recommendation, so the functional form is the ITU anchor and its use on a facade is an extrapolation made here.
source.why_this_file_exists: Recommendation ITU-R P.2040-4 (09/2025) tabulates permittivity and conductivity and deliberately supplies no facade roughness. Its layered-slab model in section 2.2.2 assumes smooth planar parallel interfaces, the only RMS height it uses is the corridor waveguide attenuation term of section 2.2.3.1 equation 48, and its one surface-scattering model in section 2.3 is a deterministic periodic array of circular cylinders rather than a Gaussian random surface. It also carries no reference list. Verified against the in-force PDF.
source.companion: config/itu_p2040_4.json supplies the dielectric side. This file supplies the roughness that semantic_twin/materials.py refuses to default.
source.units: rms_height_mm, plausible_range_mm, correlation_length_mm and mean_texture_depth_mm are millimetres. The loader converts to metres.

two_scales.headline: The single most important thing in this file. Material finish and facade structure are different physical quantities that share a symbol, and they differ by two orders of magnitude.
two_scales.sample_scale: rms_height_mm describes a prepared, monolithic patch of the material with no joints: the finish a profilometer sees. Almost every measured number in the literature is this. At 28 GHz almost every one of them is radio-smooth.
two_scales.wall_scale: A metre-scale facade patch, which is what a fishnet face actually stands for, additionally carries mortar joints, course relief, block relief, pointing, sills and reveals at centimetre pitch. That structure supplies essentially all of a real wall's diffuse power and it is periodic, not Gaussian. It is recorded in periodic_component, not folded into rms_height_mm.
two_scales.which_applies: For a metre-scale patch the wall scale governs. rms_height_mm alone is correct only for a monolithic pane such as a glazing unit or a single metal panel.
two_scales.do_not_average: The two scales must not be averaged or reconciled into one number. Doing so produces a value that describes neither.

uncertainty_note: rms_height_mm is the median of a lognormal, not a measured constant. The specular fraction is exponential in the square of the RMS height, so collapsing this prior to its median before tracing gives an answer far from the ensemble mean. Sample it.

evidence_grades.measured_mmwave: RMS height measured by independent surface metrology on the named material, with a millimetre-wave or terahertz measurement on the same physical sample.
evidence_grades.measured_metrology: RMS height measured by surface metrology on the named material, no radio measurement on that sample. Biased low whenever the instrument cut-off sits below the 1 mm to 50 mm lateral band a 28 GHz wave responds to.
evidence_grades.inferred_radio: Derived from a radio measurement through the model stated in the entry. An inversion, not a measurement.
evidence_grades.extrapolated: No measurement on this material at any frequency. Engineering prior anchored to a neighbouring class, with log_standard_deviation widened to say so.

circularity_warning.why: Several widely reproduced tables of 'typical RMS surface heights' are the output of a least-squares fit of roughness jointly with permittivity to the authors' own reflection data, and are restated downstream without that qualifier. Using such a value as a physical prior in a twin that then predicts reflection double counts the radio evidence. No entry in this file takes its central value from a radio-fitted source. Where a radio-fitted number is recorded for comparison, radio_fitted is true and it is excluded from the prior.
circularity_warning.separate_failure_mode: Distinct from the exemplar-material case, where a table of illustrative numbers never claimed to be measurements is later cited as data. Both are recorded in ROUGHNESS.md and kept apart.

structures.gaussian_random: Height field is plausibly a zero-mean random surface. The Rayleigh closure applies, subject to the validity limits below.
structures.periodic_dominant: Height variation is dominated by a deterministic repeating structure whose pitch is many wavelengths. Such a surface diffracts into discrete orders. The Gaussian coherent fraction does not describe it and the entry's rms_height_mm describes only the face between the repeating features.
structures.two_scale_periodic_plus_random: Random micro-roughness on the face of each unit, plus a periodic between-unit structure. Both scales are recorded and neither alone is the answer.

closure_validity.note: Three independent limits on exp(-g^2), all established from primary sources. All three push the same way: real surfaces keep more specular power than the Gaussian closure predicts.
closure_validity.non_gaussian_heights: The factor is the squared characteristic function of the height distribution. Below g^2 of about 3 the shape is worth less than a factor of two; above it the shape dominates. g^2 = 3 is 1.48 mm at 28 GHz and 0.69 mm at 60 GHz, both at normal incidence.
closure_validity.empirical_breakdown: Independently, an empirical test against deposited goniometer data over 50 materials finds the Ament factor unbiased to a Rayleigh exponent of about 2 to 3 and over-predicting the specular loss by 12 to 20 dB beyond it. Two unrelated routes landing on the same threshold.
closure_validity.correlation_length: The Kirchhoff derivation requires the surface correlation length to exceed the wavelength. Measured correlation lengths for plaster and wallpaper are 1.3 to 2.3 mm, so the constraint is met only above 130 to 230 GHz. At 28 and 60 GHz the closure is outside its own stated validity range for those materials.
closure_validity.consequence: Treat exp(-g^2) as reliable where g^2 < 3 and as a labelled approximation elsewhere. gaussian_closure_reliable_28ghz records this per class at normal incidence, which is the worst case.

sensitivity.note: Computed from the model above, reproduced in ROUGHNESS.md.

irrelevance_threshold_um.comment: RMS height below which the specular loss is under one percent at normal incidence. Classes under this line do not need an accurate roughness value at all.

half_power_rms_mm.comment: RMS height at which half the specular power is gone, normal incidence.

classes.name: glass_glazing_unit
citations: Jensen, Fojan, Jensen, Gurevich, 'Surface characterization of coated and uncoated float glass', River Publishers, 2013. AFM: air side Rq 0.4 plus or minus 0.3 nm, tin side 0.7 plus or minus 0.4 nm, with the tin side confirmed by EDX.

Taleb, Hernandez-Cardoso, Castro-Camus, Koch, IEEE Trans. Terahertz Sci. Technol., doi:10.1109/TTHZ.2023.3281773, deposited data at doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.21539109: white and black glass coupons, sigma 0.005 mm and correlation length 1.5 mm by photogrammetry over 5 by 5 cm, with radio on the same coupon from 105 GHz to 1.05 THz.
classes.note: Float glass is roughly four orders of magnitude below the 85 micrometre irrelevance threshold at 28 GHz, so the value is immaterial and that is the finding. The central value is set at 1 micrometre rather than 1 nanometre because a real window carries dirt, sealant and a coating. A glazed facade's radio behaviour is set by the slab, the low-emissivity coating and the mullion grid, none of which is roughness. Do not spend calibration effort here.

classes.name: metal_cladding_panel_smooth
citations: Watkins et al., Coatings 13(6):982, 2023, doi:10.3390/coatings13060982: pigmented polyurethane coil coating on hot-dip galvanised steel, Ra 0.41 plus or minus 0.02 micrometres by stylus, so Rq = 1.2533 times 0.41 = 0.51 micrometres for Gaussian heights. Clearcoat 0.46 micrometres Ra, Rq 0.58 micrometres.
Evin et al., Processes 13(2):450, 2025, doi:10.3390/pr13020450: electro-discharge-textured cold-rolled sheet specified at Ra 1.0 to 1.7 micrometres, Rq about 2.0 micrometres.
classes.note: Measured but with the standard cut-off trap: both sources use a 0.8 mm filter, so they see none of the 0.8 to 30 mm band a 10.7 mm wave responds to. The central value is inflated ten times above the measured 0.5 micrometres to allow for that unmeasured band, and even so the class is radio-smooth by a factor of seventeen. What would actually break specularity on a metal panel is panel-scale waviness, oil-canning and fixing dishing of tenths of a millimetre over 0.1 to 1 m. That is deterministic geometry, not roughness, and no metrology addresses it.

classes.name: render_plaster_painted
citations: Piesiewicz, Jansen, Mittleman, Kleine-Ostmann, Koch, Kurner, IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag. 55(11):3002-3009, 2007, doi:10.1109/TAP.2007.908559, Tables I and II, read in the full PDF. Two concrete plaster samples, optical 3D micro and nanometrology with a 5x objective at 25 micrometre lateral and 5 micrometre vertical resolution, Gaussian fitted to the measured zero-mean height histogram. sigma = 0.05 mm (s1) and 0.15 mm (s2), correlation length 1.3 mm and 1.7 mm. Radio measured separately at 100 to 1000 GHz on the same samples.
Taleb et al. figshare deposit: gypsum plaster and gypsum board coupons at sigma 0.128 and 0.183 mm.
Alissa, Friederich, Sheikh, Czylwik, Kaiser, IEEE Access 8:170672-170680, 2020, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2020.3025361, Table 1: wallpaper 0.074 to 0.145 mm by laser confocal microscopy under ISO 25178.
classes.note: Read the grade carefully. There is no metrology anywhere for exterior cement or lime render, stucco, roughcast or painted render: a dedicated search returned zero numeric values, not weak ones. Every number here is an indoor plaster or gypsum sample. Piesiewicz is the provenance anchor for the whole metrology strand because its roughness is instrumented independently of its radio data, which is exactly what the circular chains lack, and it measures concrete plaster. Two cautions beyond that. The samples are prepared laboratory plates, so these values are a lower bound on a weathered European render rather than a central estimate. And roughcast or pebbledash is dominated by 6 to 10 mm chippings and is a deterministic geometric scatterer at 10.7 mm, not a perturbative rough surface, so this class does not describe it at all.

classes.name: concrete_as_cast_smooth
citations: Kozubal et al., Materials 13(11):2542, 2020, doi:10.3390/ma13112542: concrete cast against formwork, sigma_h about 0.10 mm from a semivariogram sill of 0.0102 to 0.0112 mm^2, by close-range photogrammetry over 110 by 110 mm at 0.067 mm spacing. The same fit gives a spherical semivariogram range of 4.47 to 5.01 mm, which is the correlation length recorded here and the most defensible facade-adjacent pair of surface statistics found anywhere in this exercise.

Czarnecki, Materials 18(23):5320, 2025, doi:10.3390/ma18235320: areal ISO 25178 over 50 by 50 mm at 0.1 mm spacing with no filter, so genuinely in the radio band. Steel-trowelled Sq 0.242 plus or minus 0.053 mm, ground Sq 0.122 plus or minus 0.012 mm, shot-blasted Sq 0.370 plus or minus 0.056 mm. The same source measures Sq/Sa at 1.326 against the Gaussian 1.2533, so concrete heights are mildly non-Gaussian and the Gaussian conversion under-predicts.

Yoshino, Chakarothai, Inagaki, Kawanishi, IEEE Access, 2026, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3681775: concrete plate sigma 101 micrometres, measured with a KEYENCE VHX-8000 digital microscope, with permittivity from a separate THz time-domain spectrometer and the scattering data used as a forward check. Roughness, correlation length and permittivity are each obtained independently, so this entry is not circular.
Taleb et al. figshare deposit: Beton concrete coupon sigma 0.075 mm, correlation length 1.99 mm.
classes.note: Four independent metrology sources span 0.075 to 0.242 mm and the central value sits in the middle. All are laboratory or prepared specimens, so this is the finish of concrete cast against formwork and a lower bound on a weathered facade. Beware the dominant concrete-metrology tradition, which splits the profile at a 0.8 mm filter and reports the sub-0.8 mm part as roughness: that convention gives as-cast concrete a few micrometres and would wrongly make it perfectly specular. The waviness band, not the roughness band, is what a 10.7 mm wave responds to. Yoshino's correlation length of 0.25 mm is forty times below the wavelength, so the Kirchhoff assumption behind the closure is violated even though g^2 is small enough that the numerical answer barely moves.

classes.name: concrete_board_marked_or_exposed_aggregate
citations: Kozubal et al. 2020: sandblasted concrete sigma_h 0.49 to 0.70 mm with an exponential semivariogram range of 8.64 and 10.41 mm, the closest measured analogue to a textured architectural finish.
Czarnecki 2025: shot-blasted concrete Sq 0.370 plus or minus 0.056 mm.

Sezen and Fisco, J. Civ. Eng. Manag. 19(3), 2013, doi:10.3846/13923730.2012.746237: exposed-aggregate concrete pavement at an estimated texture depth of 1.87 mm, a mean profile depth of about 2.07 mm after inverting ASTM E1845.
classes.note: Extrapolated, wide prior. No metrology exists for board-marked, bush-hammered or exposed-aggregate architectural concrete. The central value is bracketed by sandblasted concrete at 0.49 to 0.70 mm below and pavement exposed aggregate well above. This entry sits squarely in the band where the answer is most sensitive, 0.6 mm costs 39 percent of the specular power at 28 GHz normal incidence, so it is the first place to spend a measurement.

classes.name: brick_face
citations: Taleb et al. figshare deposit doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.21539109: fire clay brick coupon sigma 0.024 mm, correlation length 2.35 mm, photogrammetry over 5 by 5 cm with radio on the same coupon.

Alissa, Friederich, Sheikh, Czylwik, Kaiser, IEEE Access 8:170672-170680, 2020, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2020.3025361, Table 1: brick sigma 0.095 mm by laser confocal microscopy, five 7 by 7 mm patches under ISO 25178.

Pascual-Garcia et al., IEEE Access 4, 2016, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2016.2526600, Table 1: brick Ra 14.68 micrometres by Talysurf CLI optical profiler under ISO 4287, so Rq = 1.2533 times 14.68 = 18.4 micrometres.

Arnold et al., Remote Sensing 13(4):789, 2021, doi:10.3390/rs13040789: extruded ceramic block laying face, areal Sa 2.27 micrometres over 48 patches at 10 micrometre pitch, so Sq about 2.85 micrometres.

Cross-check by inversion, performed here and not published: NYURay calibrated reflection losses (arXiv:2410.03104 Table X) of 12.8 dB at 73 GHz and 18.9 dB at 142 GHz against a smooth normal-incidence Fresnel reference of 9.68 dB imply 0.276 mm and 0.245 mm. Those are wall measurements, not coupons, and they land an order of magnitude above the coupon metrology.
classes.note: This entry describes the face of a brick, not a brick wall. Use brick_wall_with_mortar_joints for a facade patch. Four metrology sources span 0.003 to 0.095 mm and every one of them is radio-smooth at 28 GHz. An important limitation: all of them measure die-extruded structural blocks or laboratory coupons, and no metrology was found for a sand-faced, wirecut, handmade or weathered architectural facing brick, which is what a Ghent facade is. The wide log standard deviation carries that gap. The radio inversion lands ten times higher precisely because it measures a wall rather than a brick, which is the two-scale split appearing inside a single material.

classes.name: brick_wall_with_mortar_joints

specular_fraction.comment: Face only. The wall's diffuse behaviour is set by the joint grid and is not described by these numbers.

periodic_component.description: Bed-joint grid. Deterministic, so it diffracts into discrete orders rather than producing a smooth diffuse lobe.
periodic_component.dimensions_status: UK Brick Development Association, Designing to Brickwork Dimensions, 2023: work size 215 by 102.5 by 65 mm with a nominal 10 mm joint, giving a 75 mm vertical course pitch and a 225 mm horizontal stretcher pitch. Recess depth from BDA Mortar for Brickwork, 2023: recessed joints should not exceed 4 mm, the only hard numeric depth found in a citable standard. WARNING: the 75 mm course pitch is British. Belgian and Dutch waalformaat and lagenmaat give a different course height and it was not verified. Propagating-order count scales directly with pitch, so this must not be averaged over.
periodic_component.unit_scatter_note: BS EN 771-1 dimensional tolerance class T2 is plus or minus 4, 3 and 2 mm and class T1 is plus or minus 6, 4 and 3 mm, with range class R1 at 9, 6 and 5 mm. Brick-to-brick face-plane offsets of several millimetres therefore exist even in flush work. This is a genuinely random wall-scale term, it is a hundred times the brick-face roughness, and it is the random part of a brick wall that actually matters at 10.7 mm.

citations: Face roughness as for brick_face.

Landron, Feuerstein, Rappaport, IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag. 44(3), 1996, Table I, read in the full PDF: a real brick wall characterised as maximum roughness height h = 1.3 cm and sigma_h = 0.5 cm, with eps_r 4.44. Wall scale, two orders of magnitude above the coupon.
classes.note: The class where the two-scale split matters most, and the one that should drive the propagation design. The brick face is radio-smooth at 28 GHz by a factor of thirty, so essentially none of a brick wall's diffuse power comes from surface finish. It comes from the joint grid at roughly seven wavelengths pitch, which diffracts into about fifteen discrete orders rather than a smooth lobe, and from several millimetres of unit-to-unit face-plane scatter. Representing either as a Gaussian sigma gets the magnitude and the angular distribution wrong. specular_power_fraction refuses without allow_periodic for this reason.

classes.name: stone_ashlar_dressed

periodic_component.description: Ashlar coursing. Dressed stone is laid with fine joints, so the grid is weaker than brick but still deterministic.
periodic_component.dimensions_status: engineering prior from typical dimension-stone coursing. No standard obtained.

citations: Molina et al., Front. Mater. 7:581979, 2020, doi:10.3389/fmats.2020.581979: areal ISO 25178 by focus-variation videomicroscopy, eight samples per finish. Saw-cut, honed and bush-hammered Sa for calcarenite 0.27, 0.23 and 0.42 mm, travertine 0.24, 0.22 and 0.38 mm, sandstone 0.18, 0.16 and 0.28 mm, arkose 0.23, 0.21 and 0.30 mm. Multiplying by 1.2533 gives Sq of 0.20 to 0.53 mm. After accelerated sulphur-dioxide ageing every value rises 10 to 25 percent.

Yoshino et al. 2026: granite plate sigma 336 micrometres with a correlation length of 1.69 mm as printed, which is 1.33 mm once corrected from the paper's 0.2 autocorrelation threshold to the conventional 1/e definition.

Lopez et al., Coatings 9:131, 2019, doi:10.3390/coatings9020131: polished granite Ra 0.068 and 0.22 micrometres, so Rq 0.085 and 0.28 micrometres, but at a 0.25 to 0.8 mm cut-off and therefore a lower bound.

Cross-check by inversion, performed here: NYURay Table X gives an outdoor granite reflection loss of 6.9 dB at 28 GHz against a smooth Fresnel reference of 6.87 dB for the ITU marble row, that is no detectable excess.
classes.note: The central value is the areal Sq of sawn and honed sedimentary stone, which is what a European ashlar facade usually is. Note a factor of fifty in the literature that is mostly instrumental rather than physical: sawn granite reads a few micrometres at a 0.8 mm stylus cut-off while sawn limestone reads 200 to 300 micrometres areal with no filter. Use the areal numbers and treat every stylus number as a lower bound. Polished granite really is three orders of magnitude smoother and sits far outside this prior. Two further limits: nothing measures rock-faced or split-face stone, and for cleaved natural stone a single correlation length is not merely unmeasured but the wrong model, because the measured power spectrum shows no roll-off at all from 60 micrometres to 20 mm.

classes.name: stone_rough_rusticated

periodic_component.description: Rusticated or rubble coursing. Block relief is the dominant term and it is quasi-periodic rather than random.
periodic_component.dimensions_status: from Landron's described limestone wall, blocks averaging 0.5 by 0.3 m with relief features up to 12.7 cm.

citations: Landron, Feuerstein, Rappaport, IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag. 44(3), 1996, Table I, read in the full PDF: rough limestone wall, maximum roughness height h = 12.7 cm, sigma_h = 2.5 cm, eps_r = 7.51, with the body text describing blocks averaging 0.5 by 0.3 m. The paper calls these estimated roughness parameters and does not state the method, but they are a physical characterisation of the wall rather than a fit to the radio data, which the paper's stated purpose of comparing measurement against theory would have defeated.

Dillard, MS thesis, Virginia Tech, 2003, Table 4.2: 28 GHz perpendicular reflection coefficients for a real limestone wall, inverted against smooth Fresnel to an implied sigma of about 1.3 mm at 5 degrees falling to about 1.0 mm at 45 degrees, with the angle convention verified as being from the normal.

Persson et al., J. Phys. Condens. Matter 17:R1, 2005, doi:10.1088/0953-8984/17/1/R01, Figures 7 and 8: cleaved basalt and granite show a self-affine power spectrum with no roll-off across 60 micrometres to 20 mm and a fractal dimension near 2.0.
classes.note: The widest prior in this file and the least satisfactory entry. Two wall-scale sources disagree by a factor of twenty: Landron's 25 mm at 1.9 and 4.0 GHz gives a specular fraction of zero at 28 GHz to machine precision, which is not a useful model output, while Dillard's 28 GHz inversion on a comparable wall gives about 1 mm. The gap is the two-scale problem in its sharpest form and it is not resolved here. Persson's result additionally says that for cleaved stone the single-correlation-length Gaussian model is structurally wrong and a self-affine spectrum is needed.

classes.name: wood_cladding

periodic_component.description: Board coursing and shiplap or feather-edge overlap.
periodic_component.dimensions_status: engineering prior from typical timber cladding profiles. No standard obtained.

citations: Kerzic et al., BioResources 16(3):4675, 2021, doi:10.15376/biores.16.3.4675-4692: areal confocal over 3.6 by 5.9 mm with no filter. Machined spruce and larch Sa 20.6 and 8.7 micrometres, so Sq 25.8 and 10.9 micrometres. After 9, 18 and 27 months of natural outdoor weathering spruce Sa rises to 30.3, 42.2 and 53.1 micrometres, so Sq 38.0, 52.9 and 66.6 micrometres.
Yoshino et al. 2026: wood plate sigma 48.9 micrometres with a correlation length of 67 micrometres as printed, 53 micrometres once corrected to the 1/e convention.
Alissa et al. 2020 Table 1: four wood samples at 0.012 to 0.050 mm, dark oak 0.047 mm, laminate 0.052 mm.
classes.note: The central value is weathered rather than freshly machined, because a facade is weathered: 27 months outdoors roughly triples spruce Sq. Two systematic biases both point upward. Wood-science roughness is deliberately anatomy-stripped, so a published wood Rq is a lower bound for radio because the wave sees the vessels and latewood the algorithm removes. And weathering roughness lives above about 0.26 mm lateral scale, so a 0.8 mm cut-off measurement misses most of it. Even so the class stays radio-smooth at 28 GHz, and the board-overlap step is the larger effect. Yoshino's correlation length of 53 micrometres is two hundred times below the 28 GHz wavelength, the most severe Kirchhoff validity violation in this table.

classes.name: metal_profiled_sheet

specular_fraction.comment: Sheet face only, meaningless for the corrugation.

periodic_component.description: Corrugation or slat pitch. A conducting periodic profile of this pitch is a reflection grating, and it is the entire radio behaviour of the surface.
periodic_component.dimensions_status: engineering prior consistent with the periodic attribute already recorded in config/semantic_concepts.json for corrugated sheet and roller shutters.

citations: Watkins et al., Coatings 13(6):982, 2023, doi:10.3390/coatings13060982: pigmented polyurethane coil coating on hot-dip galvanised steel, Ra 0.41 plus or minus 0.02 micrometres by stylus, so Rq = 1.2533 times 0.41 = 0.51 micrometres for Gaussian heights. Clearcoat 0.46 micrometres Ra, Rq 0.58 micrometres.
Evin et al., Processes 13(2):450, 2025, doi:10.3390/pr13020450: electro-discharge-textured cold-rolled sheet specified at Ra 1.0 to 1.7 micrometres, Rq about 2.0 micrometres.
classes.note: The clearest case in the table. The sheet itself is a mirror and every non-specular effect comes from the profile, which is deterministic and known once the pitch is estimated. Modelling this with a roughness coefficient discards information the semantic layer can actually supply.

classes.name: ceramic_tile_facade
citations: Anchored to the glazed-surface coupons in the Taleb deposit, which run 0.005 to 0.024 mm for glass and polished marble.
classes.note: A glazed tile is a fired glass surface and is radio-smooth. This class has no ITU-R P.2040-4 dielectric row either, as config/semantic_concepts.json already records, so it resolves the surface without resolving the material.

classes.name: asphalt_road_dense_graded
classes.mean_texture_depth_status: Sand-patch mean texture depth from Kurz et al. It is a volumetric quantity, not an RMS height, and it is recorded here without conversion.
citations: Bitelli, Simone, Girardi, Lantieri, Sensors 12(7):9110, 2012, doi:10.3390/s120709110, Tables 3 and 4: dense-graded asphalt concrete mean profile depth 0.65 mm and profile Ra 0.41 mm from triangulation laser scanning of Italian in-service and cored specimens. Rq = 1.2533 Ra gives 0.514 mm for Gaussian heights.

Same source, Table 4: areal skewness +2.24 and kurtosis 9.72, so the heights are strongly non-Gaussian and leptokurtic, which makes the true Rq larger than the Gaussian conversion and 0.514 mm a lower bound.

Independent route: the published relation SMTD = 0.6 times mean profile depth, where sensor-measured texture depth is defined as the standard deviation of the profile, from Freitas, Pereira, Antunes, Domingos, 2008, Figure 9, R-squared 0.9. That gives 0.39 mm.
Kurz et al., Adv. Radio Sci. 19:165, 2021: eight German road surfaces measured at 77 GHz with sand-patch mean texture depth on the same surfaces, asphalt concrete 500 micrometres.
classes.note: Two independent routes give 0.39 and 0.51 mm and the central value splits them, with the correlation length carried over from the stone mastic measurement because none exists for dense-graded. The prior is the narrowest in this file because the pavement literature is standardised and large. Three caveats. The heights are demonstrably non-Gaussian, areal skewness plus 2.24 and kurtosis 9.72, so the Gaussian conversion is a lower bound. ASTM E1845 low-pass filters below 2.5 mm, so the mean-profile-depth route omits the finest band. And the measured power spectrum of pavement rolls off at 4 mm to 1 cm, which sits directly on top of the 28 GHz wavelength, so this is the one class where the surface spectrum and the wavelength are genuinely comparable.

classes.name: asphalt_road_coarse
classes.mean_texture_depth_status: Sand-patch mean texture depth for stone mastic asphalt from Kurz et al. Not an RMS height and not converted.
citations: Auriacombe, Vassilev, Pinel, J. Infrared Millim. Terahertz Waves 43:108-124, 2022, doi:10.1007/s10762-022-00847-5, section 2.2, read in the full open-access PDF. Stone mastic asphalt with about 8 mm aggregate, scanned with a Handyscan 3D laser scanner at 0.025 mm accuracy over a 50 by 50 mm area chosen to match the radiometer beam spot. RMS height 0.65 plus or minus 0.03 mm and correlation length 2.54 plus or minus 0.03 mm, with a Gaussian fitted to the height density at R-squared 97.32 percent and to the correlation function at R-squared 99.27 percent. Radiometric measurement on the same surface at 50 and 56 degrees.

Bitelli, Simone, Girardi, Lantieri, Sensors 12(7):9110, 2012, doi:10.3390/s120709110, Tables 3 and 4: stone mastic asphalt mean profile depth 0.97 mm and Ra 0.51 mm, so Rq 0.639 mm; open-graded asphalt 1.54 mm and Ra 0.79 mm, so Rq 0.990 mm.
Kurz et al., Adv. Radio Sci. 19:165, 2021, Table 1: SMA8 800 micrometres and SMA11 810 micrometres sand-patch depth on real German roads measured at 77 GHz.
classes.note: The single best-evidenced entry in this file, and the only one where an independently measured RMS height, a measured correlation length, a stated Gaussian goodness of fit and a millimetre-wave measurement all exist on the same physical surface. Bitelli's independent Rq of 0.639 mm agrees to two percent. The Gaussian fit at R-squared 97 percent also means the non-Gaussian caveat that troubles the facade classes does not bite here. Kurz back-solves a smooth-surface permittivity from the same 77 GHz band and obtains 8.3 to 10.4 for asphalt and 1.87 for whisper concrete, both far outside plausible bulk values, which is what unmodelled roughness loss does to a smooth-Fresnel inversion. That inference is drawn here and is not the authors' claim.

classes.name: concrete_paving_slab

periodic_component.description: Unit grid. Joints are tight and level steps are small, so at 28 GHz this is close to a smooth surface with a weak lattice.
periodic_component.dimensions_status: Belgian Standaardbestek 250 v4.1a Hoofdstuk 6 sections 3.4.3.8.A and 3.4.3.5, read in full text by a subagent: concrete block joints at most 3 mm laid straight and 6 mm in tight curves, level step between adjacent units at most 2 mm. Clay pavers per sections 3.6.3.9.A and 3.6.3.6 are the same.

classes.mean_texture_depth_status: Estimated texture depth for burlap-drag concrete from Sezen and Fisco, converted to a mean profile depth by inverting ASTM E1845, not converted to an RMS height.

classes.note: The worst case for the Gaussian model in this file. Three separable scales: a lattice at 100 to 160 mm pitch, which is 9 to 15 wavelengths at 28 GHz and diffracts into roughly 25 discrete orders; deterministic level steps of 6 to 10 mm, which is 0.56 to 0.93 wavelengths, so the step-to-step phase is structured rather than randomising; and genuine random relief of up to 10 mm on each riven face. Only the third is a legitimate sigma. The rms_height_mm above is the face relief expressed as a standard deviation and it is the only one of the three the closure can carry.
